## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāḷiyajātaka* (Ja 367) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon, titled *The Hedgehog* in English translation. According to the narrative framework recorded in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the Buddha delivered the discourse while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana), prompted by the remark that Devadatta could not even cause fear or alarm (*āvuso Devadatto tāsakārako pi bhavituṁ nâsakkhi*) [Fausböll 1883]. The story of the past is set in Bārāṇasī during the reign of King Brahmadatta, where the Bodhisatta was born into the family of a landowner (*kuṭumbiyakula*), opening with the verse beginning *Yo 'yaṁ sāliyachapo* [Fausböll 1883]. The title also appears listed in the *Dhammapada* commentary tradition [Burlingame 1921].
